content:
Hi everyone,

I've been experimenting with introducing a scoped notation for Algebra.adjoin to make adjoining elements a bit more ergonomic and closer to what I would write on paper. My initial thought was to use standard brackets, allowing us to write R[a] or R[a, b] as shorthand for Algebra.adjoin R {a} and Algebra.adjoin R {a, b}.

The implementation i have in mind would mimic the one from IntermediateField.
See #35928 and this example.

I know the immediate concern here is the overlap with Polynomial (A[X]), List, and GetElem. However, after some testing, I feel like it shouldn't cause too many issues in practice - but I could be wrong. Currently, if both Polynomial and Algebra are open R[X] is always interpreted as Polynomial R.

That said, I know parser ambiguity can be a headache to maintain. If standard brackets are considered too risky or contentious, I am completely open to just use some other kind of brackets.

What are your thoughts? Is it worth trying [] scoped to Algebra, or is it better to just play it safe and use some other type of brackets?

Also, if there is interest in this I think we should do something for RatFunc K as well!
are you aware of the notation for adjoining one element?
oh no, I seem to have mixed up IntermediateField.adjoin and Algebra.adjoin, there doesn't seem to be any notation for Algebra.adjoin

I think that it is worth doing the experiment, especially as you've already identified some potential risk. If all goes through nicely it would be a great improvement, so keep track of these experiments.
Why not use ⟮α⟯ like we do for intermediate fields?

This would be an option but would have, in my opinion, two disadvantages:

  • We would not be able to use the two adjoin notation in the same section/theorem.
  • Using brackets [α] I think aligns more with the usual notation for Algebra.adjoin while ⟮α⟯ are closer to parentheses (field adjoin) which I think was the goal. It is after all not a coincidence that polynomials use brackets.
This should have a more specific scope than just Algebra, such as probably Algebra.AdjoinNotation

Aaron Liu said:

oh no, I seem to have mixed up IntermediateField.adjoin and Algebra.adjoin, there doesn't seem to be any notation for Algebra.adjoin

There's one in RingTheory/Conductor.

This is now #35928 that looks very nice to me. My only concerns was that this is same notation as polynomials but it seems to work (in the sense that polynomial wins and nothing special happens). Unless someone sees a real problem here I am going to merge it later today.
